Rulebook solo setup: a Dummy player. You choose your Tactic first, it draws one at random, and both are removed for the rest of the game. Remove the four interactive Spells (no. 17 to 20) and your Hero's interactive Skill.

Rulebook co-op setup: a Dummy player, which draws its Tactic at random before you. At the end of each Round, remove from the game one of the Tactics used by the players. Remove the four interactive Spells (no. 17 to 20) and each Hero's interactive Skill. No combat between players.
Blitz scenario bonuses: you start with 1 Fame and 2 Reputation; each new line reached on the Fame track gives 1 extra Fame; one more die in the Source and one more Unit in the Offer.

Score: your Fame, the Achievements without titles, then 10 points per conquered City, 15 more if all are conquered, 30 per unused Round, 1 per card left in the Dummy's Deck and 5 if the end of the current Round hadn't been announced.

Team score: the Fame of the player furthest behind, then for each Achievement the better of the two players, without titles. Add 10 points per conquered City, 10 if each player is Lord of at least one City, 15 if all are conquered, 30 per unused Round, 1 per card left in the Dummy's Deck and 5 if the end of the current Round hadn't been announced.
The rulebook allows any scenario to be played solo with the Solo Conquest setup, without stating the number of tiles for one player: this companion uses the values for 2 players.

Revealed Mine, including on tiles placed during setup: place an Enemy token face up on it, green on a Countryside tile, red on a Core tile, and a brown token face down. Arrange them so the brown one stays clearly visible: they aren't rampaging enemies. If brown tokens run out, draw them only when revealing them.
Liberating a Mine is your action, by entering its space: you fight both enemies with Night rules, as in a Dungeon, but your Units take part. A survivor stays in place and can be attacked later.

Whoever eliminates the last enemy liberates the Mine: Shield token and +1 Reputation (+2 on a Core tile). A Mine produces nothing while occupied; once liberated, it produces right away: a Crystal at the end of this turn.
At the start of each Round, each liberated Mine gives a Crystal of its colour to whoever liberated it, wherever they are.
Ending your Movement in a Magical Glade lets you activate it: place a Shield token there. It isn't an action. A Glade can hold several Shields, one per player.
Once during the first Night, on a space that isn't an inhabited site, you can perform an incantation: it is your action. Draw a brown monster per Glade you have activated and fight them.

Each defeated monster earns double its Fame. The others vanish at the end of the combat, but their Wounds remain. Each summoned monster, defeated or not, gives at the end of the turn a Crystal rolled on the die, as in a Monster Den.
At the end of the first Night, remove all Shields from the Glades: they must be reactivated for the second incantation.
Second Night: a new incantation, this time with red enemies. Double Fame, and two Crystals per summoned enemy.
Homemade scenario, written for this companion and not playtested at the table: adjust freely if it turns out too hard or too easy.
Volkare replaces the Dummy player and counts as a player: the Source holds real players + 3 dice, the Units Offer real players + 3 cards.

Volkare's Deck: the 16 Basic Action cards of an unused Hero, the four interactive Spells (no. 109 to 112) and Wounds depending on the Pursuit Level. It is never reshuffled. Replace the interactive Skills with the cooperative Skills; in solo, add to the common Offer a Skill from another randomly drawn Hero after each of your Levels.
Tactics: the players choose first, then Volkare draws his from the remaining ones. In solo, your Tactic is removed from the game at the end of the Round; in co-op, none are.

Fighting Volkare means facing his whole army plus his own attack, rolled on the die, always Brutal and Assassination. Volkare can't be targeted: he is defeated when all his troops are. They aren't Fortified, except in a fortified site or across a Wall.

With two players, you can attack or defend together: split the elite troops (white and red) on one side and the regulars (grey and green) on the other, then each fights their share and suffers Volkare's attack.
Volkare never announces the end of the Round and doesn't play a last turn. Each turn, he reveals a card: the companion tells you what to do.

As long as the City isn't revealed, Volkare explores according to his cards. As soon as it is, he heads there by the shortest path. Each Wound revealed can make a Wavering Unit leave the Offer, adding a grey token to his army.

When Volkare, adjacent to the City, must advance, he assaults it. Unconquered City: you lose. Conquered but undefended City: he plunders it, and the second time you lose. If you defend it and he loses at least one token per player, he falls back one space.
Open board limited to 4 columns; Volkare's Camp is the leftmost starting tile, and its space has no effect.
Board shape set by the rulebook, Volkare's Camp opposite the Portal. All tiles are placed face down, except the Camp, the Portal and the 3 tiles touching it.
City and Volkare levels, Wounds in his Deck and marked Units: set in the Game tab, based on the Combat and Pursuit Levels.
Victory as soon as Volkare's whole army is eliminated. Defeat if he reaches the City before you, plunders it twice, or if the last Round ends.

Team score: the Fame of the player with the least Fame, the best player's Achievements per category, without titles, and 20 points if the City is conquered. Volkare defeated: 30, 40 or 50 points depending on the Combat Level, plus 2 per card left in his Deck, bonus multiplied by 1, 1.5 or 2 depending on the Pursuit Level.

Volkare marches towards the Portal without revealing tiles. When he comes within 3 spaces of the Portal, it closes: it becomes an ordinary space, and a player on it is out of the game. Revealed Wounds make Frightened Units leave the Offer, without reinforcing his army.
If Volkare loses, before his turn, at least twice as many tokens as there are players, he skips his next turn: don't touch his turn button that time.
Victory as soon as Volkare's whole army is eliminated. Defeat if he enters the Portal and then must advance again.

Team score: the Fame of the player with the least Fame, the best player's Achievements per category, without titles, and 5 points per conquered City. Volkare defeated: 30, 40 or 50 points depending on the Combat Level, plus 2 per card left in his Deck, bonus multiplied by 1, 1.5 or 2 depending on the Pursuit Level.

Dummy player. You choose your Tactic first, it draws one from the remaining ones, and both are removed from the game at the end of the Round. Remove the four interactive Spells (no. 109 to 112) and replace the interactive Skills with The Lost Legion's cooperative Skills.

Dummy player, which draws its Tactic at random before you. You form a single team. Remove the four interactive Spells (no. 109 to 112) and replace the interactive Skills with The Lost Legion's cooperative Skills.
Faction Leader: you must enter its space, which isn't safe, to face it with its followers. Each attack equal to its Armor removes one level; the details are in the tutorial, chapter "Tezla: Leaders".
Score: your Fame and the Achievements, without titles.
Team score: the Fame of the player with the least Fame, and for each Achievement the best player, without titles.
Add 1 point per card left in the Dummy's Deck and 5 if the end of the current Round hadn't been announced.
High-level start: each Hero starts at Level 3 with 9 Fame, and builds a Deck and an army with 18 Influence, following the rulebook variant.

The Cities are destroyed: no figure and no card. Only one figure per City space, and entering it costs 2. Place a Draconum face down there, revealed as soon as a player is adjacent, by Day or Night. It isn't rampaging: entering the space means fighting it. If you win, you find the fragment and mark the space with a Shield.

Rampaging Draconum on City tiles are replaced by green rampaging enemies. Remove the Elite Units only recruitable in a City. One more die in the Source and one more Unit in the Offer. +1 Fame per line reached on the track, +1 per Core tile revealed, and another +1 if it has a ruined City.

Gather all the Elementalist tokens into one pile: rampaging enemies come from it and, except those placed at setup, gain Ambush. Defeating a rampaging Elementalist makes you add a Core tile, like an exploration, not necessarily next to you.

Exploring costs triple, and you can pay this cost with Influence. When the white City tile is placed, the Forgotten Valley covers the City space, with the High Priestess and her followers. The Keep on this tile is guarded by 2 green Elementalists. The Valley has no effect before it is liberated.
Gather all the Dark Crusader tokens into one pile: rampaging enemies come from it. Those that an exploration brings out during your turn receive your Shield and Pursue you from the following turn.
Each revealed Magical Glade becomes a Graveyard, with face-down enemies depending on the order of discovery: two green; one green and one brown; one red; one green and one red; one brown and one red.

Liberating a Graveyard is an action, from its space; survivors remain. Reward by order: Advanced Action, Spell, Unit, Artifact, then Artifact and Advanced Action. Then, on the spot, spend a mana to seal it, without an action: Shield and +1 Reputation. When the blue City tile is placed, the Necropolis covers the City, with the Necromancer.

Sort the green, brown and red tokens by Faction. Rampaging enemies come from the Dark Crusaders on the Northern tiles, from the Elementalists on the Southern ones, and from a Faction rolled on the die in between; the rulebook diagram shows which tiles are North and South.

Magical Glade revealed on a Countryside tile: in the South, two Elementalists, one green and one brown, face up; in the North, a Graveyard and two Dark Crusaders; in between, a random Faction. Liberating the place is an action: you fight both enemies, gain an Artifact (Glade) or a Spell (Graveyard), place a Shield and gain 1 Reputation. Before liberation, the place has no effect.

The green City isn't placed in the North, the red one not in the South. The Forgotten Valley covers the green City and houses the Elementalists' Leader; the Necropolis covers the red City and houses the Dark Crusaders' Leader. The third City is friendly.
Quests module required (sheets 7 to 10 of the Game aid), in Normal mode by default. The City levels shown already take the quests into account: no +1.
Helping hand: a Hero on the same space as another can, during their own turn, produce part of the non-combat values (Block, Move, Influence, Healing…) required by their ally's quest.
A site only offers quests once for the whole team.

Solved if the goal is reached. To compare your games: your Fame and the Achievements without titles, plus 5 points per quest completed at tier I, 10 at tier II, 15 at tier III, and 30 per unused Round.

The Shadow Brotherhood

Honest folk close their doors to you, but the Brotherhood always has work for a Knight without scruples. Take a City and become its shadow agent.
The revealed City is level 5.
Path of shadow: when a quest offers 😇 or 😈, you always choose 😈.
Shady contacts: as long as your Reputation gives you a penalty, on each draw, you may replace the result of one of the two rolls with ⚫.
Reminder: with a penalty Reputation, Monasteries are closed to you, and in a conquered City you can only accept a ⚫ quest.
As soon as the third ⚫ quest is completed, if one is tier III, play one last turn. Otherwise at the end of the fifth Round. Your Reputation must then give you a penalty.

Dungeon Lords
Reveal all tiles and conquer all Dungeons and Tombs.
A network of tunnels links Dungeons and Tombs. Five Rounds: three Days, two Nights.
8 Countryside tiles: only remove tiles without a Dungeon.
The Blue City Core tile, plus 1 Core tile without a City: the Desert tile with no Monastery or Tomb.
The Blue City is friendly: place a Shield token on it, nobody is its Lord.
When you reveal a Village, choose an adjacent accessible space, with no site and not a Swamp: it is the secret entrance of a Dungeon. Place a brown token face down there.
When you reveal a Monastery, do the same with a red token: it is a secret Tomb.

Secret Dungeons and Tombs follow the normal rules for these sites: Night rules, no Units. If you fail, the token is discarded and replaced with a new one, face down. Once conquered, there is no more fighting there.
From a Dungeon or a Tomb, you can reach any other already conquered one for 2 Move points plus 1 per space of distance, going around lakes and swamps.
When everything is revealed and conquered, you play one last turn.
Your Fame and the Achievements; each Dungeon or Tomb, secret or not, counts 4 points instead of 2.
